channel.title: Wire — Frontend
channel.description: Frontend from thirty sources, one digest a day.

item.title: Button Sounds: Tactile SFX for Your UI
item.description: A free collection of 50+ professionally-recorded multi-sampled clicks and toggles. Distributed via NPM. (2 sources: frontendfocus, hackernews)

item.title: Bypassing iOS Safari's 60 FPS Limit for Canvas
item.description: Getting iOS Safari web apps to a full 120 Hz, input and rendering, using native scroll containers and OffscreenCanvas. (3 sources: hackernews, javascriptweekly, lobsters)

item.title: Nudeps: Bundler-Like Imports, None of the Baggage
item.description: Bundlers are currently the only way to use dependencies without losing our sanity, but introduce complexity and overhead. Today, I’m releasing a new type of lightweight build tool that challenges that. (2 sources: frontendfocus, javascriptweekly)

item.title: Web Dependencies are Broken. Can We Fix Them?
item.description: Dear JS ecosystem, I love you, but you have a dependency management problem when it comes to the Web, and the time has come for an intervention. (2 sources: frontendfocus, javascriptweekly)

item.title: takes it for a spin here
item.description: Ladybird is an astonishingly ambitious project: a new browser, in 2026, with its own implementation of most of the key components—HTML parsing, CSS engine, layout, JavaScript, even WebAssembly. It still … (2 sources: frontendfocus, javascriptweekly)

item.title: Why there are still no non-WebKit browsers on iOS
item.description: Years after Apple allowed alternative browser engines on iOS in the EU, still no browser has launched there with an engine other than WebKit. (3 sources: frontendfocus, hackernews, lobsters)

item.title: Show HN: Old Nvidia and ATI tech demos, running again in the browser
item.description: Graphics card demos by 3dfx, NVIDIA and ATI from 1998 to 2006, running in the browser. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: Things You Can Do With a Browser in 2027
item.description: Things you can do with a browser in 2027 ☕️. Contribute to luruke/browser-2027 development by creating an account on GitHub. (1 source: frontendfocus)

item.title: When Everything Has Changed, What Do We Do Next?

item.title: GitHub Ditches CSS-in-JS for CSS Modules, Reports 55% Faster SSR After Three-Year Migration
item.description: GitHub migrated github.com from styled-components to CSS Modules over three years, reporting a 55% cut in server-side rendering time and 25% faster component initialisation. (1 source: infoq)
